unlisted_practices: Regulators should create a new regulatory category for large language models distinct from already regulated AI-based medical technologies.
Regulators should provide guidance for companies and healthcare organizations on deploying LLMs into their existing products and services.
Regulators should create a framework covering future multimodal LLM iterations such as sound and video analysis, not only text.
Regulators should distinguish between LLMs trained specifically on medical data and LLMs trained for non-medical purposes.
Regulators should regulate companies developing LLMs, similar to the FDA Digital Health Pre-Cert Program, rather than every LLM iteration.
Regulators should mandate diverse and representative data sources for AI training data to counteract bias.
Regulators should incorporate continuous monitoring and evaluation mechanisms for LLMs.
Regulators should involve patients at the highest level of decision-making in regulating LLMs (patient design).
Healthcare professionals and patients should be made aware of AI involvement in decision-making and be given explanations for AI recommendations.

Regulators should focus on concrete high-risk LLM applications rather than the pre-trained model itself, with obligations for transparency, risk management, non-discrimination, and content moderation.
Regulators should develop new auditing procedures that capture the risks posed by LLMs.
